what_happened: Job 20261027-011733-vrsk ("Move Transport row from gh/mod.rs to gh/transport.rs", a G2 retry) ended failed because the producer made no change. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria, no blocker or major findings and no failed checks. Nothing was produced, and the event doesn't say why. The Transport row may have already been moved, the producer may have been unable to find it, or it may have stopped without doing the work. The work was not judged.
cause: Athena treats an empty producer diff as a bare failure. The producer isn't required to say whether the work was already done, blocked, or abandoned. Nothing checks before dispatch that the thing to be moved is still where the request says it is, in the current snapshot. A retry also doesn't carry over what the earlier attempt (G2) did or didn't land. So a no-op run looks the same as a crash, and the operator can't tell a stale request from a producer fault without digging. The class is a bounded job that has no way to stop with an explanation.
prevention: Two code checks. (1) Before dispatch, resolve each named source symbol and file in the current snapshot (here the Transport row in gh/mod.rs and the target gh/transport.rs). If the source is absent or the target already holds it, mark the job already-satisfied or stale and don't run a producer. (2) Make an empty-diff producer finish with a required structured reason (already done, blocked with the blocking fact, or could not locate the code). Record that reason on the failed job and don't accept a bare 'made no change'.
proposed_request: Make Athena explain and prevent empty producer runs on bounded code jobs. Outcome: (1) Before a code job's producer is dispatched, Athena resolves each source symbol and file the request names against the job's snapshot. If the thing to move is already at its target, the job ends as already satisfied with that evidence. If the source can't be found, it ends as a stale request naming the missing path. In neither case does a producer run. (2) When a producer ends with no change, the job records a required reason, one of already done, blocked (with the blocking fact), or could not locate the code. The failed-job event shows that reason instead of only 'the producer made no change'. (3) A retry's reading carries forward what the earlier attempt landed or left, so a retry such as G2 starts from the current state. Acceptance: a test with a request whose Transport row is already in gh/transport.rs ends as already satisfied with no producer run; a test with a missing source ends as stale naming the path; a test where a fake producer returns an empty diff with no reason is rejected and with a reason is recorded in the event. Then re-run the G2 job: Move the Transport row from gh/mod.rs to gh/transport.rs without changing behavior, with the existing tests passing.
